newsitem.title: ISRAEL: U.S. Mideast envoy makes little progress.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Mideast envoy makes little progress.

text.p: U.S. Middle East envoy Dennis Ross appeared to be making little progress in his latest mission to revive Israeli-Palestinian peace negotiations.
"I cannot tell you that I am optimistic," Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu told reporters on Thursday.

Peace talks between Israel and the Palestinians broke down two months ago after Netanyahu gave the final go-ahead for the construction of 6,500 houses for Jews in Arab East Jerusalem on land claimed by both sides.

Netanyahu and Jordan's King Hussein met secretly in Jordan later on Thursday to try to patch up a row over water and to discuss reviving the Israeli-Palestinian talks, the newspaper Yedioth Ahronoth reported on Friday.

The king has in the past played a broker's role between Netanyahu and Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat. But the daily, Israel's biggest, gave no indication progress was made on peacemaking or the water dispute.
Jordan's Crown Prince Hassan cancelled a meeting with Netanyahu on Tuesday because of disagreements over water supplies Israel promised Jordan under a 1994 peace treaty.
Ross, on his second Middle East mission in a month, met Arafat in Gaza and Netanyahu in Jerusalem on Thursday.
Chief Palestinian negotiator Saeb Erekat told Israel Radio that the U.S. envoy brought no new ideas.
Ross was due to meet Arafat again on Friday and then go to Cairo, ending his current round of talks ahead of Israel's memorial and independence day commemorations on Sunday and Monday.

A Moslem militant blew up a Tel Aviv cafe in March, killing himself and three Israeli women, and Israel says Arafat must crack down on such "terror" attacks before resuming talks, a move which Netanyahu said "would help the peace process".

Arafat's spokesman Marwan Kanafani said the Palestinian leader stressed to Ross the need to stop all Jewish settlement activity before peace talks could resume, but Netanyahu's aide David Bar-Illan said the building work would continue.
Erekat said Arafat gave Ross documents on Israeli settlement activities on land captured in the 1967 Middle East war.
"We told Ross: Examine this report. You will find that Netanyahu is negotiating through the bulldozers," Erekat told the radio.
Israel appeared to lend little weight to a meeting which Bar-Illan said its Shin Bet domestic security chief would hold with his Palestinian counterparts on Friday, with U.S. officials sitting in.
"There were meetings like this one in the past," Naveh said.
Israel has demanded a resumption of full security cooperation suspended by the Palestinian Authority, which is in charge of self-ruled parts of the West Bank and Gaza.

Jewish settlers said shots were fired late on Thursday at an Israeli vehicle carrying 11 Jewish female students on the road between Jerusalem and the West Bank town of Hebron. The army said bullets hit the van but no one was hurt.

In a move that angered the Palestinians, Jewish settlers took up residence in a house on Jerusalem's Mount of Olives. An Armenian cleric sold the villa, on Israeli-annexed land, to an American Jew who leased it to the settlers.
